story.headline: Goalposts in a river last time: No. 7 Alabama heads back to Vanderbilt
paragraphs: Alabama and coach Kalen DeBoer can't escape the memories of the Crimson Tide's last visit to Vanderbilt even with all the roster changes in the transfer portal era.

The last time the Crimson Tide played on Vanderbilt's home field, the Commodores posted an upset so historic fans celebrated by tearing down the goalposts and dumping them in a river two miles from campus.

“This is a different team than we had last year, which is different than the year before, too,” DeBoer said ahead of Saturday's game. "So, we gotta take our experiences from what we’re going through right now and apply them.”

No. 7 Alabama (7-2, 5-2 Southeastern Conference) is coming off a 31-13 win at LSU that pushed the Crimson Tide up to third in the College Football Playoff rankings. Alabama is second in the SEC standings behind only Georgia thanks to the head-to-head tiebreaker over Kentucky.

story.headline: No. 6 Indiana faces No. 15 USC in high-stakes game with Big Ten title game, playoff implications
paragraphs: No. 6 Indiana and No. 15 USC understand the high-stakes game they're playing Saturday.

But instead of getting caught up in the hype of what may appear to be a must-win scenario, the defending national champions and the Trojans want to keep this simple and avoid thinking about the long-term ramifications of a single game.

“To be honest with you, we're not focused on the Big Ten championship at all,” Hoosiers receiver Charlie Becker said. “We're really focused on USC. The Big Ten championship, if we're going to get there, we've really got to focus on winning each game and right now our opponent is USC. IF the Big Ten championship (game) comes then we'll focus on that.”
